meta.description: Orchestrator. Resolves client config ONCE from Notion, runs Module 1, then ROUTES on the request type (pricing_only | proposal_only | full_pipeline): a price-only request runs Module 3 and drafts a quote; a proposal-only request runs Modules 2+4 (no pricing); a full request runs Modules 2 ∥ 3 then Module 4. Effective route = the request's own request_type, falling back to the client's default service_tier. Incomplete RFQs branch to a Telegram review alert. NOTE: after import, repoint each 'Call Module N' Execute Workflow node to the deployed sub-workflow (by name) and link credentials.

filters.q: subject:(RFQ OR presupuesto OR proposal OR quote OR estimate)

parameters.content:
## 00 — Orchestrator (resolve-once + request routing)
**Load Client Registry → Map Client Config** resolves `client_config` ONCE (resolve-once) — including `service_tier` and `pricing_sheet_id` — and passes it through every module.

**Call Module 1 → RFQ Complete?**: if Module 1 flags the RFQ `incomplete`, **RFQ Needs Review** (Telegram) fires and it stops. Otherwise **Resolve Route** picks the effective route — the request's own `request_type`, falling back to the client's `service_tier` — and **Route by Request Type** (Switch) branches:
- **pricing_only** → Module 3 → **Build Quote Draft** → Gmail draft + Telegram (a price estimate, no document).
- **proposal_only** → Module 2 → Module 4 (document with NO pricing block).
- **full_pipeline** → Module 2 ∥ Module 3 → merge → Module 4 (full document).

Pricing inputs are entered manually and **filtered by the request's scope of supply** (phase 1 has no auto hours-estimation engine). ⚠️ After import, repoint each **Call Module N** node to the deployed sub-workflow (by name) and link Gmail/Google/Anthropic/Telegram/Notion credentials.
